newsitem.title: UK: Charlton Athletic FC seek AIM listing.
newsitem.headline: Charlton Athletic FC seek AIM listing.

text.p: English first division soccer club Charlton Athletic are seeking to raise some five million stg through an AIM listing, the club said on Tuesday.
The south-east London club said it intended to use the majority of the funds to finance the development of the main West Stand at its home ground, The Valley.
The stadium capacity should rise from 15,000 to 20,000 once the stand has been rebuilt. A planning application has already been submitted.
The flotation is expected to go ahead in the next couple of months and value the club at between 10-20 million stg.
The bulk of Charlton's shares are held by its directors.
"The flotation marks the next stage of the development of Charlton Athletic, following our successful return to The Valley four years ago," chairman Richard Murray said.

"The completion of the West Stand on our freehold site will make The Valley a stadium for the club to be proud of. The board of Charlton Athletic feel that our renowned youth policy will continue to contribute significantly to the further success of the club," he added.
The club returned to its traditional home stadium in 1992, after sharing grounds with London rivals for several seasons.
The funds to finance the purchase of the stadium and redevelop it were largely provided by Charlton shareholders, who subscribed for over seven million stg of equity.
Charlton were in the old first (now Premier Division) from 1986 to 1990 but their glory days are in the more distant past.

They played in two consecutive F.A. Cup finals in the immediate post-war era, losing to Derby County in 1946 and beating Burnley in 1947. The Valley was one of England's largest football stadiums at that time, drawing crowds of up to 75,000.

Charlton's board said the club, currently mid-table in the first division, would continue to strive for promotion. It noted that nearby Greenwich was the centre of England's Millennium celebrations, which it said should attract a lot of investment to the area.
